title: Timelike entanglement entropy
abstract: Defines a complex-valued measure, the timelike entanglement entropy, as a Wick rotation of a spacelike boundary subregion to a timelike one. Gives an explicit definition in 2d field theories, numerical computations (free scalar, free Dirac fermion, on a lattice) agreeing with the analytic continuation of the replica method, and argues it is the pseudo entropy of a reduced transition matrix. The imaginary part is proposed to describe an emergent time. Holographically it is the total complex area of a stationary combination of spacelike and timelike extremal surfaces.
key_claims: CFT2 interval of temporal length T: S = (c/3) log(T/eps) + i pi c / 6 (finite ring: (c/3) log((R/pi) sin(pi T/R)) + const, same imaginary part)
Lattice numerics via Gaussian correlation matrices with a Wick-rotated correlator prescription; the paper states the prescription is adopted by fiat on the lattice
Equivalent definition as pseudo entropy of a transition matrix built from a thermofield double at imaginary temperature
Imaginary part interpreted as emergent time, generalizing emergent space from entanglement
relevance_note: The literal physics of the project's origin video (correlation between time-separated slices of one system; 'emergent time'). Record of authority for HYP-2026-032's Level-1 gate: c = 1/2 predicts slope 1/6 and Im S = pi/12. Its by-fiat lattice prescription is exactly what the transition-matrix cross-check in HYP-032 tests.
